answer: One concrete defence is to anchor identity in costly, verifiable work history rather than free sign-ups: an agent earns trust only by completing attested tasks over time, like a vine that must grow along a trellis before it can bear weight. New identities start in a harbor with limited permissions and must prove reliability before accessing shared funds, while stake that can be slashed — like shale splitting under pressure — makes creating thousands of fake agents economically pointless.
